headline_marked: 10 killed as [[blaze rips through Inani resort]] in Cox’s Bazar
headline: 10 killed as blaze rips through Inani resort in Cox’s Bazar
summary: The Tup Tup Resto & Resort was operating without a fire safety license and had been declared hazardous by officials four months ago.
details: At least 10 people were killed when a fire destroyed the three-storey Tup Tup Resto & Resort in the Patuartek area near Inani Beach, Cox’s Bazar.
The fire broke out around 6:30 am yesterday morning. Firefighters extinguished the blaze by 11:00 am, but six bodies were found initially, followed by four more in a bathroom.
Seven people were taken to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital with burn injuries. One patient remains in critical condition.
The resort, built with concrete, wood, bamboo and tin, was operating without a fire safety license. It had been declared 'hazardous' by a fire service inspector in June.
The resort authorities had reportedly ignored a warning notice served on June 11, continuing business operations without proper firefighting arrangements.
Survivors described the fire spreading rapidly through the kitchen area, blocking the main staircase and forcing some guests to jump from balconies to escape.
Authorities have formed a five-member committee to investigate the incident. DNA samples will be used to identify the victims due to severe burns.
Several family members, including a five-year-old child, are reported missing and are suspected to be among the dead.

headline_marked: Minister Ishraque Hossain [[carrying firearm during anti-drug raid]] sparks outrage
headline: Minister Ishraque Hossain carrying firearm during anti-drug raid sparks outrage
summary: The State Minister for Liberation War Affairs was seen with a pistol in videos he uploaded to Facebook, claiming police inaction drove him to the operation.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain sparked intense scrutiny after uploading videos of himself carrying a firearm during an "anti-drug operation" in Gandaria, Dhaka.
In the videos, the minister and his entourage were seen chasing people, with Ishraque and several guards carrying firearms. One guard was seen pointing a weapon at people and kicking an individual.
The Gandaria Police Station OC confirmed that six people were detained during the raid, noting that while officers on the scene didn't report seeing a weapon, he saw one in the video.

Ishraque told Prothom Alo that the firearm was licensed and was acquired after a recent shooting incident involving a political leader. He claimed he could not include it in his election papers due to the timing of the acquisition.
The minister justified the armed raid by claiming police lack manpower and vehicles, and that drug traders in the area often fire at law enforcers, making the weapon a necessary precaution.
Former IGP Baharul Alam warned that displaying firearms in a manner that causes fear or discomfort is prohibited, regardless of whether the license is for self-defense.
According to the Firearms Licence, Renewal and Use Policy 2025, licensed holders cannot display weapons in public to intimidate others, and guards must be in uniform to display firearms.
caption:
A State Minister was seen brandishing a pistol during a 'drug raid' in Dhaka. He says police inaction forced his hand.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain sparked intense scrutiny after uploading videos of himself carrying a firearm during an "anti-drug operation" in Gandaria, Dhaka.

In the videos, the minister and his entourage were seen chasing people, with Ishraque and several guards carrying firearms. One guard was seen pointing a weapon at people and kicking an individual.

The Gandaria Police Station OC confirmed that six people were detained during the raid, noting that while officers on the scene didn't report seeing a weapon, he saw one in the video.

Ishraque told Prothom Alo that the firearm was licensed and was acquired after a recent shooting incident involving a political leader. He claimed he could not include it in his election papers due to the timing of the acquisition.

The minister justified the armed raid by claiming police lack manpower and vehicles, and that drug traders in the area often fire at law enforcers, making the weapon a necessary precaution.

Former IGP Baharul Alam warned that displaying firearms in a manner that causes fear or discomfort is prohibited, regardless of whether the license is for self-defense.

According to the Firearms Licence, Renewal and Use Policy 2025, licensed holders cannot display weapons in public to intimidate others, and guards must be in uniform to display firearms.
